rows.34:9560:
...Where is that Rubelize now, you ask?
I heard it was put in Okawa's grave.{p}
rows.34:95d0:
Apparently she died with the Rubelize clutched tight in her hand.
So it was buried in the grave along with her.
Oh, yes. Fujiomi, you know... he's still alive.
Okazaki was hopeless too, wasn't she?
Imagine leaving alone the very first person she should have cursed.
I wonder if she's so consumed with bitterness that she can't tell one from the other anymore.
...Well, never mind.
It has nothing to do with me.{p}
rows.34:974c:
By the way, this story is going in the school paper, isn't it?
I do hope nobody who reads it gets the idea of taking the Rubelize that's in Okawa's grave for themselves.
Heh heh...
That's the end of my story.
...Still, the seventh one is awfully late, aren't they?{p}What will you do, {a}{f:|}?
It's about time we went home, don't you think...?{p}
rows.34:9874:
If you don't know, I'll tell you.
Okawa tried to steal the Rubelize from Okazaki's grave.
I wonder what kind of nerve that girl had.
She seemed to think stealing from the dead was fine, as long as nobody found out.{p}
rows.34:9b48:
I think graveyards are frightening even in the daytime.
And this was the middle of the night.
A high school girl, all alone.
That's not something just anyone could do.
And her purpose was grave robbing, at that.
Okawa must have had nerves of steel.
Or perhaps the Rubelize sleeping in the grave was calling her to it.
Heh heh...
Either way, she moved the gravestone aside and took Okazaki's urn out from inside.{p}
rows.34:9ca4:
And when she opened the urn...
"Aaah!☆"
There was no Rubelize in there at all.
All that was inside were fragments of burnt bone and ash.
"Wh-why...?"
For a moment, Okawa was at a loss.
But then she thought it over.
If the Rubelize had been burned along with Okazaki's body...
then the Rubelize really was in this urn after all, wasn't it?
So she took the ashes from the urn home with her.
She really had some nerve, didn't she?
That's not how a normal person thinks.
Well, I suppose it just shows how badly she wanted the Rubelize.{p}
rows.34:a004:
And in the ghost's hand was a pendant that looked like the Rubelize...
The ghost said,
"You fool, Okawa.
The Rubelize was never buried with me.
But, well, never mind.
In honor of your persistence, I'll make you a present of it..."
Hearing that, Okawa drifted unsteadily toward the ghost.
Thoughtless, I suppose you'd call it.
And she reached out her hand to take the Rubelize.
And then...{p}
rows.34:a1b0:
"Gyaaaah!☆"
Okawa was strangled.
By Okazaki's ghost.
With the Rubelize's pendant chain...{p}
rows.34:a4a4:
You see, they say Okazaki never once used the Rubelize's power.
At the prices back then, the Rubelize was worth enough to buy a house.
So it was kept carefully locked away in a safe.
That's why, even though she knew what it could do, she never asked it for a single wish.
Apparently her parents meant it to be part of her trousseau when she married.
Though, of course, Okazaki died before that could happen.
In a traffic accident.
The rumors everyone spread were just the facts with a tail tacked on.
So what does that make Okawa, who let them lead her around by the nose?
They say the Rubelize pendant wasn't in the room where Okawa died.
Okazaki's ghost must have taken it back home with her.
I imagine it's back in the safe at her house again by now, don't you?{p}
rows.34:a86c:
Okazaki, you see, was the daughter of quite a powerful zaibatsu family.
And her father acquired the Rubelize on a trip abroad.
They say it was worth enough to buy a house even at the prices back then, so as a little souvenir from abroad, it's far beyond anything people like us would call normal.
She adored that stone.
Back then, nobody paid any mind yet to the idea that it was a stone that brought happiness.
But since it was a rare stone even by world standards, it seems it became the talk of the school.
And the girls who told Okawa about her must have heard that rumor from somewhere too.
Okazaki was a true young lady of good family.
She'd never known hardship, and she'd been raised with great care, so she was gentle and honest by nature.
To put it kindly, she was pure.
To put it unkindly, she had no sense of caution, I suppose.
To anyone looking on, she was truly happy.
She grew up with all her father's love lavished on her alone, and her classmates fawned over her, too.{p}
rows.34:b8e8:
She had it made into a pendant.
They say she treasured it.
And whenever she wished she could see that girl again, she would squeeze the Rubelize tight.
As if she were asking the Rubelize for a favor.
And then...{p}
rows.34:baf4:
After that, Okazaki often made her way to the music room to listen to the organ.
Making a wish on the Rubelize each time.
Because when she did, she could always see that girl she had never been able to meet before.
Every time, Okazaki listened to her play and spent moments that felt like a dream.
Okazaki lived a life of luxury, but she had her own troubles too.
Friendships at school, her studies, the loneliness of having no mother...
At times like that, she always comforted her heart with the sound of that organ.{p}
rows.34:be74:
One day, Okazaki came to the organ without making a wish on the Rubelize.
The music room was filled with the smell of the building's wood.
The organ stood there in silence.
"I wonder what it would sound like if I played it..."
As if drawn in, she went up to the organ.{p}
rows.34:c894:
That night, Okazaki lay on her bed, thinking.
What had that girl been?
Through the Rubelize's power, she'd learned the girl wasn't human, but...
Was she a ghost...?
If so, whose ghost could she be?
Okazaki's thoughts raced.
Just then...{p}
rows.34:cce8:
Then suddenly the light went out.
A woman's low voice rang out, as if shaking the bed.
"Yukie.
Stop going to the music room.
Or you'll be cursed to death.
Understand? ...Listen carefully.
You told the Rubelize you wanted to know who the girl playing the organ really is.
She is..."
Just then, the sound of an organ came from somewhere.
And besides the low woman's voice, she heard a beautiful woman's voice.
That voice had a clear ring to it that was somehow nostalgic.{p}
